rounds.scripted_answer: Default arguments are evaluated once when Python defines a function. A default list is shared across calls, so appending mutates later results. Use None as the default, then create a fresh list inside the function when the argument is None. Test two calls without an argument and check that their lists are independent. Lists and dictionaries are mutable; tuples are immutable but may contain mutable objects.
